correctness.rationale: With at most three ones, a three-block Abelian cube has exactly zero or one one in each block. The all-zero factors are the distinct cubes of lengths 3t in a longest zero gap. A three-one factor contains the same unique three marked ones and is determined by its start and block length; solving the three block-position constraints gives the claimed integer interval exactly. Counting the same factors by (start, block length, one-position per block) gives the exact t^3 population sum and rational generating function. The uniform gap-composition simplex limit and uniform Riemann approximation give the Dirichlet functional. A complete finite pairwise-interval inequality reduction gives z<=3y,3y-x<=2, and integrating the joint density six of three ordered uniforms gives 7/9. The independent direct checker verified every one of 17,550 three-one words through length 26, population sums, and the exact 2/9 atom.

value.rationale: This is the smallest positive binary Hamming weight at which an Abelian cube can contain ones in all three blocks. It gives an exact count for every word, a rational all-length aggregate generating function, and a nontrivial scaling limit with explicit expected value 1/270 and exact atom 2/9. The sharp 7/9 limiting existence probability answers a natural sparse-repetition question and distinguishes structural freedom from avoidance results. No claim of a full all-weight theory or a paper-sized downstream advance is needed.
